jobs.title: Drift Wood #6 · the Thanksgiving issue
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 17, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers, a bristol pad clutched flat to his chest, chin up; CHLOE — aged 17, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders, oversized dark cardigan, a Discman on her belt with headphones around her neck, a folded-back paperback, reads while talking; GULLY — aged 18, stocky boy with a round face, backwards blue cap, faded green hoodie with his hands in the front pocket, muddy tan work boots, easy slouch. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: What are you thankful for. Wood has a list. Gully has a shorter one. Panel 1: a teenage girl with a clipboard surveying a boy in a backwards cap at a table in a school newsroom, a hand-lettered poster on the wall (in this panel: CHLOE, GULLY). Chloe says "Survey. One thing you're thankful for. Gully.". Gully says "Maple bars.". Panel 2: a teenage boy in an overcoat standing and holding up one finger mid-list, a girl with a clipboard waiting (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "The tension between the individual and the provincial. The fog. Truffaut. The fact that no one here reads, which leaves the field open—". Panel 3: close-up of a girl writing one word on a clipboard survey form (in this panel: CHLOE). Chloe says "I'm putting 'fog.'". Panel 4: a pasted-up newspaper column of student names with one word beside each, one line left blank, xerox grain. caption box: "THANKFUL FOR — THE TIMBERLINE ASKS". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
